subtitle: How a Gond warlord forged a forest kingdom of fifty-two forts

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of a hilltop fort above dark forest, storm clouds massing
panels.action: Sangram Shah stands in heavy armour on the ramparts of a stone hill-fort, the endless Satpura forests and scattered fort-crowned ridges rolling away under a brooding sky.

dialogue.text: In the deep forests of Garha-Katanga, Aman Das—called Sangram Shah—raised a Gond kingdom of fifty-two forts. How did a hill chief build a power that even the Mughals had to reckon with?

i18n.hi: गढ़ा-कटंगा के घने जंगलों में अमन दास, जिसे संग्राम शाह कहा गया, ने बावन किलों वाला गोंड राज्य उठाया। एक पहाड़ी मुखिया ने ऐसी ताकत कैसे खड़ी की कि मुग़ल भी संभल जाएँ?

panels.shot: high aerial wide over dense Satpura hills and the Narmada winding silver through forest
panels.action: An endless sea of dark-green forested hills stretches under a pale dawn, the Narmada gleaming like a silver snake between ridges, with smoke rising faintly from hidden settlements.

dialogue.text: Before Sangram Shah, the Narmada-Satpura lands were a patchwork of Gond lineages, small forts, hunting grounds and caravan paths between Malwa, Khandesh and the Deccan.

i18n.hi: संग्राम शाह से पहले नर्मदा–सतपुड़ा की धरती गोंड कुलों, छोटे किलों, शिकार के मैदानों और मालवा, ख़ानदेश, दक्खन के कारवां-रास्तों की रंगबिरंगी जाली थी।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a modest hill-fort courtyard, early-morning light
panels.action: A younger Aman Das in simple warrior dress stands in a rough stone courtyard, watching Gond archers drill while women carry grain baskets and smiths hammer spearheads nearby.

dialogue.text: Aman Das was one such Gond chief. Later inscriptions remember him as Sangram Shah, the first of his line to turn a forest stronghold into a structured state.

i18n.hi: अमन दास भी ऐसा ही एक गोंड सरदार था। बाद की ताम्र-लिपियाँ उसे संग्राम शाह कहती हैं—अपनी वंश-रेखा में पहला जिसने जंगल के गढ़ को व्यवस्थित राज्य में बदला।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Aman Das reading by lamplight in a wooden hall
panels.action: Aman Das sits cross-legged in a dim hall, a palm-leaf manuscript open before him, a Brahmin pandit pointing to a line while a lamp flickers, throwing shadows on carved wooden pillars.

dialogue.text: Court tradition remembered him not only as a fighter. He brought Sanskrit pandits to his capital and listened, night after night, as they read out lineages, dharma and the politics of kings.

i18n.hi: दरबारी कथा उसे केवल योद्धा नहीं मानती। वह अपनी राजधानी में संस्कृत पंडित बुलाता, जो रात-दर-रात वंशावली, धर्म और राजधर्म सुनाते।

panels.shot: wide shot of Singorgarh-type hill-fort from outside, rugged track climbing up
panels.action: A rugged stone fort crowns a steep hill, with a narrow path snaking up; Aman Das rides up on horseback, flanked by spear-bearing retainers and bare-chested Gond porters with bundles.

dialogue.text: Singorgarh and later Garha near Jabalpur would anchor his realm. From such hill-forts he began to knit together scattered Gond estates into one Garha-Katanga kingdom.

i18n.hi: सिंगौरगढ़, और बाद में जबलपुर के पास गढ़ा, उसके राज्य की धुरी बने। इन पहाड़ी गढ़ों से उसने बिखरी गोंड ज़मींदारियों को जोड़कर एक गढ़ा-कटंगा बना डाला।

panels.shot: overhead map-like shot with animated feel, showing forts as glowing points spreading
panels.action: A stylised view of the Narmada basin and Satpuras shows small, glowing fort symbols flaring to life across hills and river crossings, linked by faint paths as Aman Das leans over a rough map.

dialogue.text: Later memory spoke of fifty-two forts and seventy thousand villages. The numbers are formulaic, but they hint at a wide federation of strongholds across the Narmada-Satpura zone.

i18n.hi: बाद की याद में बावन किले और सत्तर हज़ार गाँवों की बात चली। गिनती चाहे रूढ़ि हो, पर संकेत था नर्मदा–सतपुड़ा भर में फैले गढ़ों के संघ का।

panels.shot: medium shot of a council hall, mix of Gond chiefs and Brahmin scribes
panels.action: In a wooden-pillared hall, Aman Das sits on a low throne, surrounded by tattooed Gond headmen with feathered turbans and seated Brahmin scribes holding writing boards and styluses.

dialogue.text: To bind these hills, he needed more than raids. He summoned Gond headmen, rewarded loyalty with shares of forest and field, and used scribes to record dues and obligations.

i18n.hi: इन पहाड़ियों को जोड़ने के लिए सिर्फ़ डाके कम थे। उसने गोंड मुखियाओं को बुलाया, वफ़ादारों को जंगल और खेत के हिस्से बाँटे, और लिपिकों से लगान और बंधन लिखवाए।

panels.shot: close-up on Aman Das listening to a messenger from the plains
panels.action: A dust-covered messenger from the Malwa plains bows before Aman Das, holding a sealed letter; Aman Das’ face is intent, the lamplight catching the lines of calculation in his eyes.

dialogue.text: Beyond the forests, Sultanates rose and fell. News came from Malwa, from Khandesh, from Gujarat. Aman Das watched these struggles and looked for chances in their quarrels.

i18n.hi: जंगलों के पार सल्तनतें उठती-गिरती रहीं। ख़बरें आतीं—मालवा से, ख़ानदेश से, गुजरात से। अमन दास इन लड़ाइयों को तौलता और उनके झगड़ों में मौके ढूँढता।

panels.shot: wide shot of a Gond warband moving through forest, spears and matchlocks
panels.action: A long column of Gond warriors moves along a forest track—some with bows, others with newly acquired matchlocks—accompanied by pack animals laden with grain and copper ingots.

dialogue.text: Garha-Katanga sat on routes between north and Deccan. By guarding passes and rivers, Sangram Shah could tax caravans, hire his men as allies, or strike when neighbours were weak.

i18n.hi: गढ़ा-कटंगा उत्तर और दक्खन के रास्तों पर बैठा था। घाटों और नदियों पर पहरा देकर संग्राम शाह कारवां से कर ले सकता था, अपने आदमी भाड़े के साथी भेज सकता था, या पड़ोसी कमज़ोर पड़ें तो वार कर सकता था।

panels.shot: medium shot at a frontier fort gate, parley scene with a plains noble
panels.action: At a fort gate, Sangram Shah meets a finely dressed plains noble; they clasp hands warily, while behind them Gond warriors and armoured horsemen eye each other across the courtyard.

dialogue.speaker: sangram_shah
dialogue.text: Your coins for our passes. Your enemies for our steel.

i18n.hi: हमारे दर्रे, तुम्हारे सिक्के। तुम्हारे दुश्मन, हमारी तलवार।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a Ramnagar-like palace wall where an inscription is being carved
panels.action: Stone-masons carve neat lines of Nagari script into a palace wall as a court official dictates; Sangram Shah stands nearby, approving, while musicians and guards wait in the courtyard.

dialogue.text: The Ramnagar inscription at Mandla would later list his line and victories, showing how his court used stone and Sanskrit to fix Gond power into the language of kingship.

i18n.hi: मandla की रामनगर शिला-लेख बाद में उसकी वंश-श्रृंखला और विजय गिनाएगा, दिखाते हुए कि दरबार ने कैसे पत्थर और संस्कृत से गोंड शक्ति को राजकीय भाषा में गढ़ा।

panels.shot: medium shot of Sangram Shah in more elaborate regalia, flanked by both pandits and tribal elders
panels.action: Sangram Shah now wears richer robes over his armour, a sword at his side; to his right stand Brahmin pandits with manuscripts, to his left aged Gond elders with hunting spears.

dialogue.text: In this forest court, Sanskrit praise met Gond custom. Sangram Shah’s state-making mixed hill traditions with the courtly forms of the wider Indian world.

i18n.hi: इस जंगल-नगरी में संस्कृत स्तुति और गोंड रिवाज आमने-सामने बैठे। संग्राम शाह की राज्य-रचना में पहाड़ी परंपरा और बड़े भारतीय दरबारों की रीति घुल-मिल गई।

panels.shot: close-up on a manuscript with the name 'Sangram Shah' and mention of Bahadur Shah being read aloud
panels.action: A pandit’s finger traces lines on a Persianate-style document as he reads; beside him, Sangram Shah listens, his face serious, the words linking his title to a distant Sultan of Gujarat.

dialogue.text: Abu'l Fazl, in Akbar’s court, would later tell a story: that Bahadur Shah of Gujarat granted Aman Das the title 'Sangram Shah', a sign that Gond and Sultanate politics touched.

i18n.hi: अकबर के दरबार का अबुल फ़ज़्ल एक किस्सा लिखेगा—कि गुजरात के बहादुर शाह ने ही अमन दास को ‘संग्राम शाह’ की उपाधि दी, निशानी कि गोंड और सल्तनती राजनीति आपस में छूती थीं।

panels.shot: tight close-up on Sangram Shah’s thoughtful face, firelight flickering
panels.action: Firelight flickers across Sangram Shah’s lined face as he sits alone at night, the distant drums of the fort fading, his eyes fixed on the darkness beyond the walls.

dialogue.text: Mughal chroniclers also told darker tales of him, of violence within his family and repentance. Modern historians treat these as court literature, shaped to moralise rather than to report.

i18n.hi: मुग़ल इतिहासकारों ने उसके बारे में काले किस्से भी गढ़े—घर के भीतर हिंसा और फिर प्रायश्चित के। आज के इतिहासकार इन्हें दरबारी कथा मानते हैं, जो उपदेश के लिए बनीं, ख़बर देने को नहीं।

panels.shot: wide shot of multiple forts being repaired and garrisons drilled
panels.action: Across several hills, different forts are shown simultaneously: walls being repaired, new wooden gates set in place, garrisons drilling in orderly ranks, smoke rising from granaries and forges.

dialogue.text: What is clearer is his work on the ground: forts strengthened, garrisons organised, revenue drawn from forest products, fields and transit, and redistributed to keep chiefs bound to his centre.

i18n.hi: जो साफ़ दिखता है, वह उसकी ज़मीन पर की गई मेहनत है—किलों को मज़बूत करना, छावनियाँ बसाना, जंगल की उपज, खेत और गुज़र-कर से लगान खींचना और उसे बाँटकर मुखियाओं को अपने दायरे में बाँधे रखना।

panels.shot: medium shot of Sangram Shah overseeing granaries and storehouses in a fort
panels.action: Sangram Shah walks through a fort’s storerooms—granaries piled high, stacks of iron, copper and textiles—while an official counts bundles and a clerk notes them on a palm-leaf.

dialogue.text: Power in these hills meant more than horses and spears. It meant stockpiled grain, iron and salt, and a system strong enough to move them where they were needed.

i18n.hi: इन पहाड़ों की ताकत सिर्फ़ घोड़ों-भालों से नहीं मापी जाती। ज़रूरत थी जमा अनाज, लोहा और नमक की, और ऐसे इंतज़ाम की जो इन्हें जहाँ चाहो, वहाँ पहुँचा सके।

panels.shot: wide shot of a fortified capital cityscape with temples, palaces and tribal quarters
panels.action: The capital spreads under the fort: a palace complex, small shrines with Sanskrit inscriptions, longhouses of Gond clans, a busy bazaar where forest produce changes hands with plains merchants.

dialogue.text: His capital showed the blend: temples with Sanskrit dedications, a palace with court rituals, and Gond quarters where clan rites continued, all under the watch of his fifty-two forts.

i18n.hi: उसकी राजधानी में यह मेल खुलकर दिखा—संस्कृत अभिलेख वाले मंदिर, दरबारी क्रियाओं वाला राजमहल, और गोंड मुहल्ले जहाँ कबीलाई संस्कार चलते रहे—सब पर उसके बावन किलों की नज़र।

panels.shot: medium shot of an older Sangram Shah blessing a younger prince or general
panels.action: An older Sangram Shah, hair streaked with grey, places his hand in blessing on the head of a younger armoured prince or commander, with a backdrop of banners and mustering troops.

dialogue.text: By the 1530s and 1540s, his line was ready to project power further. The structures he built would shape later struggles, when his successors faced the rising Mughals.

i18n.hi: १५३०–४० के दशक तक उसकी वंश-रेखा दूर तक ताकत फेंकने को तैयार थी। उसने जो ढाँचे खड़े किए, वही बाद की जद्दोजहद को आकार देंगे, जब उसके उत्तराधिकारी उभरते मुग़लों से भिड़ेंगे।

panels.shot: epic wide of a modern-like aerial view morphing back to ancient forts, symbolic
panels.action: An aerial view drifts over the same hills centuries later, scattered ruins of forts cloaked in forest, then dissolves back to the image of Sangram Shah on a rampart overlooking his domain.

dialogue.text: Today, many walls he raised lie in ruin, yet the idea he forged endures: that even in forested hills, power lasts when conquest is bound to organisation, memory and the written word.

i18n.hi: आज उसके उठाए कई किले ढह गए हैं, पर उसका गढ़ा हुआ ख़याल बाकी है—कि जंगल-पहाड़ में भी सत्ता तभी टिकती है, जब विजय का साथ संगठन, याद और लिखित शब्द दें।

title_i18n.en: Sangram Shah and the Fifty-Two Forts
